deliverables: Maintenance of existing Scalus stack and supported export targets
Dijkstra hard-fork readiness across smart contracts, transaction building, emulation, and testing
Improved interoperability with existing Cardano tooling and the broader JVM ecosystem
A first scoped application runtime validated through reference applications, integration tests, and early-user feedback
request.what: Funding for a 9-month continuation of Scalus covering maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, JVM/JS/TS interoperability, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
The proposal requests ₳2,464,844 over 9 months at a $0.16/ADA reference rate with no contingency.

The current proposal reduces the previous Scalus proposal from ₳8.5M over 12 months to about ₳2.46M over 9 months and removes the L1 node, full L2 integration, and broad formal verification from scope.
Scalus components are reused in MeshJS SDK, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
Protocols and applications including Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm are built on Scalus.
Scalus has had 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and Scalus.js reaches more than 20,000 downloads per month.

Dijkstra readiness is needed because Plutus V4, nested transactions, guard script types, and accounts affect smart contract development, Plutus evaluation, transaction building, ledger rules, testing, and developer workflows.
Delivery is milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.
Lantr Engineering claims every prior Scalus milestone was delivered on time and commits to public reporting, open community sessions, and on-time milestone delivery for treasury-funded work.
Scalus is Apache 2.0 open-source infrastructure intended for reuse across many Cardano teams, tools, and products.

summary: The document asks for ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus from July 2026 to March 2027, focused on maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped application runtime, with asserted ecosystem reuse, reduced scope from a prior proposal, and milestone-based governance.
